entries.entry_search_note: No proof found for position 1 (the father may, the exit being of value). Al-Sharḥ al-Kabīr v08:p180 and al-Mubdiʿ v06:p270 give an iḥtimāl that he may when he sees her interest in it (ḥaẓẓ), a different ground the case does not state, so it is not recorded. Also checked al-Mughnī and al-Kāfī on the father's khulʿ.

positions.who: he may, the exit being of value so that her property is not given away (a wajh some later scholars extracted; extracted also from the riwāya that the father may remit half the mahr)
it drops the mahr (a wajh: as an annulment, or as shared by both spouses since it is at her request)
halved: the cause (sabab) is his defect and she is excused (Taqī al-Dīn, from Aḥmad's answer on the majbūb in Muhannā's report)
halved (a wajh Ibn Rajab extracts from the next masʾala)
his word: he is the one liable (ghārim) and the aṣl is freedom of his dhimma (the first wajh)
the whole mahr: it fell due by the contract and no cause (sabab) of its lapse is established (the implication of Abū al-Khaṭṭāb and al-Majd)
